questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Destination to friends and family. Level of speaking English. The culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find information about different aspects regarding arriving in Amsterdam. This information was provided by University of Amsterdam, who sent e-mails about registration in the city,  health care insurance, getting enrolled at the right courses, rent a bike and stuff like that. The institute I studied under was also very helpful regarding my course regiristration before I arrived in Amsterdam.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Moreover when arriving a lot of information about events and different social things was provided quickly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I rented a room at a Dutch girl in the western part of the city. I got it through a Facebook group, which isn't the most secure way to do it. But I was luckily. I had a lovely stay in her apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Video chat with people before transferring any money to the landlord. Sign a contract. Sometimes it can also be necessary to see their ID.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
It was very difficult for me to figure out which courses I could sign up for. And moreover the registration page often didn't approve me registrations. I communicated a lot with the office about what I could and could not sign up for. 
I read a lot about the different courses, and ended up with a lot of doubt about what I could choose. The system wasn't as flexible as I would have wanted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The institute was very helpful, moreover my home university also speeded up my approval for the courses so I didn't miss the deadlines.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Mixed. I only got some of the courses I wanted, but in the end it was a fine semester with mixed courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Be aware that you can sign up for a lot more courses than just the ones in the exchange programme. 
Begin the process early, so you have time to figure out whether you can get the courses transferred to your home university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
There was a large variation between the level of courses. I found some of the economics courses fine, but the finance course was though.
The level in general compared to UCPH is a little bit under.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The teaching was hybrid. In most courses we had lectures and exercises. Moreover we had assignments through the blocks in all courses.
The largest change for me was that we had blocks, so 8 weeks of teaching and then exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Corporate finance, Development economics, Natural ressource economics, Labour economics and industrial organisation.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Labour economics

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't do any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think soccer or volleyball sounded fun, but I didn't go.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the parks, museums, go to north, visit the canals, rent a boat.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. The city is pretty similar to Copenhagen.  People bike, there a lot of ex-pates, people are very open to new people, and they speak English very well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go out for a drink with people who your sitting next to at the lectures, find a good study group.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Dutch people are very direct, so one shouldn't take there sayings to personal.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are so multicultural, which is clear a lot of places in the city - I loved that.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Prepare your courses in good time, don't plan to many visits from friends and family, remember to have fun.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is not necessary for you to get another health insurance, you are covered through the EU.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Metting new people, getting to know a new city in an intens way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being so much alone in a new city was a large challenge for me in the beginning, but turned out to be the right thing for me.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
